"If War Comes" (Om kriget kommer) was a classic Swedish brochure during the
Cold War, intended to inform all Swedish citizens about the nation's total defence
(including both military and civil defence). However, war was not the only threat
considered by Swedish total defence planners. In this report, it is shown how the
preparation for total defence also included a range of non-military threats, such as
economic and psychological warfare. The report also includes examples of earlier
discussions of challenges of threats in the grey zone. The motivation behind this
relatively complex understanding of threats in Sweden during the Cold War was
simple - to create the most resilient society possible, prepared for military as well
as non-military warfare, or a combination of both. In times of uncertainty and war
in Europe, this goal has once again become a key issue for the Swedish total
defence.
